title: FHWA National Bridge Inspection Standards as bridge inspection and inventory rail
summary: NBIS is encoded as a bridge inspection/inventory rail: it creates inspection standards and periodic inspection expectations for highway bridges, while the cube must still track whether inspections correctly identify critical members and whether recommendations are acted upon.

status_history.note: Added as structural failure lane visibility/correction rail.

claims.claim: FHWA’s NBIS page states that the standards govern safety inspections of highway bridges, that Congress originally required NBIS in 1968, and that the original standards were established in 1971.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The same FHWA page states that periodic and thorough bridge inspections are necessary for safe operation, and the page shows a recent update date of May 20, 2026.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The cube encodes NBIS as a necessary but incomplete visibility rail because I-35W and Fern Hollow show that inspection/load-rating regimes still require critical-member, load-path, and maintenance-action specificity.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

limitations: Existence of the rail does not prove signal capture, adoption, enforcement, or correction infusion.

type_payload.infrastructure_class: bridge inspection and inventory standards rail
type_payload.signal_capture_model: periodic safety inspections and standards for highway bridges
limitations: does not guarantee correct member classification, correct load rating, or maintenance action
state/local execution and oversight remain separate surfaces

Avoid implying that absence of records means absence of risk.

unknowns: Utilization, adoption, underreporting, and recommendation-closure histories are not yet extracted.
next_actions: Link infrastructure outputs to specific case recommendation-closure records.
